document.title: Ambassador Meets Taliban: We are the People
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Ambassador Thomas Simons meets Taliban Acting Foreign Minister Mullah Ghaus on 11 November. Ghaus blames Russia, Iran and India for the ongoing war. Simons says Americans are "the most religious people in the western world." Both agree a negotiated settlement is best, but communication difficulties are evident.

events.description: Ambassador Simons met Taliban acting foreign minister Ghaus; Ghaus requested US recognition and exchange of delegations.
UN-sponsored meeting between Ghaus and a representative of the Supreme Defense Council.
Taliban forced down an aircraft with Russian aircrew carrying ammunition for Rabbani's regime; crew held in Kandahar until escape in Aug 1996.
UN-sponsored meeting between Mullah Ghaus (Taliban) and a Supreme Defense Council representative.
US Ambassador Simons met Taliban's Mullah Ghaus; Ghaus argued Taliban represents will of God and people, and complained of Russian/Iranian supplies to opponents.

Ghaus presented three requests: US recognition of the Taliban interim government, a Taliban delegation to the US, and welcome for US delegations to Afghanistan; Ambassador promised to convey them to Washington.
Embassy Islamabad cabled the meeting report to Washington (DTG 120945Z Nov 96).
Ambassador Simons met Taliban acting FM Ghaus; Ghaus blamed outside interference, requested US recognition; Simons urged negotiated settlement.
Taliban forced down an aircraft with Russian aircrew carrying ammunition for Rabbani's Kabul regime.
Russian aircrew escaped captivity in Kandahar to the UAE.
Embassy Islamabad cable 09508 reporting the meeting sent to State.

relationships.detail: Taliban lumped both as opponents supplied by Russia and Iran.
relationships.quote: DOSTAM AND COMMANDER MASOOD, WHO WANT TO INCREASE THEIR MILITARY ADVANTAGE THROUGH WAR

relationships.detail: The US Ambassador met Taliban representative Mullah Ghaus in Islamabad and debated the Afghan conflict, outside supplies and negotiation.
relationships.quote: GHAUS HAD LISTENED CAREFULLY, AND NOTED IN RESPONSE THAT WHAT THE AMBASSADOR HAD SAID WAS FRUSTRATING TO HIM.

relationships.detail: Ghaus speaks for the Taliban, claiming the movement represents the will of God and people.
relationships.quote: DOSTAM AND MASOOD WILL HAVE SUBMIT TO THE WILL OF GOD AND THE WILL OF THE PEOPLE, WHICH ARE MANIFESTED IN THE TALIBAN MOVEMENT.

relationships.detail: Simons is the Ambassador at the Embassy, which sent the cable (signed SIMONS).
relationships.quote: THE MEETING WAS COURTEOUS AND CIVIL THROUGHOUT. SIMONS

relationships.detail: Ghaus took part in a UN-sponsored meeting with a Supreme Defense Council representative on Nov 7.
relationships.quote: HIS PARTICIPATION IN A UN-SPONSORED MEETING WITH A REPRESENTATIVE OF THE SUPREME DEFENSE COUNCIL ON NOVEMBER 7

relationships.detail: Ghaus's UN-sponsored meeting is tied to UN mediation; the Ambassador urged all groups to work with Dr. Holl for a negotiated settlement.
relationships.quote: WE ENCOURAGE ALL THE GROUPS TO WORK WITH DR. HOLL FOR A NEGOTIATED SETTLEMENT.

relationships.detail: Holl is the UN mediator for Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: THE UNITED NATIONS IS BEST PLACED TO HELP THEM DO SO, AND THAT WAS WHY WE ENCOURAGE ALL THE GROUPS TO WORK WITH DR. HOLL

relationships.detail: Ghaus described Dostam as a Taliban opponent seeking military advantage through war.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN ARE FACING OPPONENTS, IN GENERAL DOSTAM AND COMMANDER MASOOD, WHO WANT TO INCREASE THEIR MILITARY ADVANTAGE THROUGH WAR.

relationships.detail: Ghaus described Commander Masood as a Taliban opponent.
relationships.quote: DOSTAM AND COMMANDER MASOOD, WHO WANT TO INCREASE THEIR MILITARY ADVANTAGE THROUGH WAR.

relationships.detail: Ghaus complained of Russian and Iranian assistance to Taliban opponents, including money printed for Rabbani.
relationships.quote: THE MONEY RUSSIA WAS PRINTING FOR RABBANI

relationships.detail: Per Ghaus, Russia printed money for Rabbani and supplied heavy weapons, planes and tanks to Taliban opponents.
relationships.quote: THE MONEY RUSSIA WAS PRINTING FOR RABBANI, BUT ESPECIALLY TO HEAVY WEAPONS, PLANES AND TANKS.

relationships.detail: Ghaus accused Iran and Russia of massive assistance to Taliban's opponents.
relationships.quote: THE PROBLEM WAS MASSIVE ASSISTANCE TO OTHER GROUPS FROM RUSSIA AND IRAN.

relationships.detail: Ghaus said claims that Pakistan and the US supported Taliban were untrue.
relationships.quote: EVERYONE WAS SAYING THAT PAKISTAN AND THE U.S. SUPPORTED TALIBAN, AND YET IT WAS NOT TRUE.

relationships.detail: Taliban asked the USG to recognize its interim government and to exchange delegations.
relationships.quote: WE WANT THE USG TO RECOGNIZE THE TALIBAN'S INTERIM GOVERNMENT

relationships.quote: MASOOD FROM RUSSIA AND IRAN. TO THE TALIBAN, HE CONCLUDED, "THE MOST IMPORTANT CONDITION FOR PEACE IS TO STOP THIS INTERFERENCE."

key_claims: Taliban acting foreign minister Ghaus blamed Russian, Iranian and Indian interference for the Afghan war.
Ghaus denied Pakistan and the US supported the Taliban; Simons said the US supports no Afghan group.
Taliban said they would keep fighting until all Afghans were disarmed.
Simons urged rejection of a winner-take-all approach and support for UN mediation.
Ghaus requested US recognition of the Taliban interim government and an exchange of delegations.
Ghaus claimed the Taliban controlled over two-thirds of Afghanistan and included Uzbeks and Tajiks.
